chunks: Ibn Mahbub from Abdullah ibn Sinan said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled that the heirs inherit the blood money (diyah), except for the maternal brothers, for they do not inherit anything from the blood money.'

key_terms.الدِّيَة: Blood money (compensation for death or injury)
key_terms.الْإِخْوَة مِنَ الْأُمِّ: Maternal brothers (brothers sharing only the mother)

ai.seo_question: Do maternal brothers inherit blood money (diyah) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights Imam al-Sadiq’s (AS) application of Ali ibn Abi Talib’s (AS) judicial precedent, illustrating the continuity of legal reasoning from the First Imam to the Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt. It specifically excludes maternal brothers (*ikhwah lil-umm*) from inhering the *diyah* of the deceased, a ruling that underscores the distinct nature of *diyah* as a compensatory right rather than a standard estate share, thereby differentiating it from general inheritance laws.
